questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a set of ordered pairs represents a function by checking for repeated x-values
questions.question: Is the relation {(3, 5), (7, 14), (7, 12)} a function?

options.label: A
options.text: No, the x-value 7 has two different y-values.

options.label: B
options.text: It cannot be a function because it has more than one ordered pair.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, every x-value has a unique y-value.

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, because every y-value has a unique x-value.

questions.explanation: The x-value 7 appears paired with two different y-values (14 and 12), so this relation is not a function.
questions.hint: Check whether any x-value in the set of pairs is repeated with a different y-value.

questions.learningObjective: Recall the graphical test used to determine whether a relation is a function
questions.question: What test can be used on a graph to determine whether a relation is a function?

options.label: A
options.text: There is no graphical test; you must check every point algebraically.

options.label: B
options.text: The horizontal line test: if any horizontal line crosses the graph more than once, it is not a function.

options.label: C
options.text: The vertical line test: if any vertical line crosses the graph more than once, it is not a function.

options.label: D
options.text: The diagonal line test: if any diagonal line crosses the graph, it is not a function.

questions.explanation: The vertical line test works because a vertical line represents a single x-value; if it crosses the graph twice, that x-value has two y-values, violating the function definition.
questions.hint: Think about what a vertical line represents: a fixed x-value across all possible y-values.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the vertical line test to a specific described graph
questions.question: Applying the vertical line test, does the graph of a straight line with slope 2 represent a function?

options.label: A
options.text: It depends on which vertical line is chosen.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, every vertical line crosses it at most once.

options.label: C
options.text: The vertical line test does not apply to this type of graph.

options.label: D
options.text: No, some vertical line crosses it more than once.

questions.explanation: For a straight line with slope 2, every vertical line intersects the graph at most once, so it passes the vertical line test and is a function.
questions.hint: Imagine sweeping a vertical line across the graph and count how many times it can cross at a single x-value.

questions.learningObjective: Determine that a circle equation does not define y as a function of x
questions.question: Does the equation \( x^2 + y^2 = 36 \) (a circle) represent y as a function of x?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, because every x-value gives exactly one y-value.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, because the equation is written with y by itself.

options.label: C
options.text: It depends on the radius of the circle.

options.label: D
options.text: No, because most x-values correspond to two y-values (positive and negative).

questions.explanation: Solving for y gives \(y = \pm\sqrt{36 - x^2}\), so for most x-values there are two possible y-values, failing the vertical line test.
questions.hint: Try solving the equation for y and see how many y-values result for a typical x-value.
